trace.query: What should I do during a typhoon?

SECTION: SAFETY GUIDE: WHAT TO DO IN A TYPHOON
SAFETY GUIDE: WHAT TO DO IN A TYPHOON
Source: announcement channels from the maintainer (September 2026); safety steps are general disaster-safety guidance, NOT an LSPU-LB protocol. Who decides suspensions and the campus's own typhoon procedure were not supplied here (see the Student Handbook rules on suspension of classes).
Before: check the official LSPU-LB Facebook page for campus-wide class suspensions, and your professor's Messenger group and Google Classroom for class-level announcements, before you travel. Keep your phone charged.
If you are already on campus in strong wind or heavy rain: stay indoors, keep away from windows and glass doors, stay out of open areas and away from trees, posts and loose signs, and follow the guards and faculty.
Do not travel through flooded roads or walk under fallen wires. Go home only when it is safe, and check announcements before coming back to campus.

primarily to assure the safety of students upon the advent, usually unexpected calamities, and forces of nature such as typhoons, earthquakes, and any untoward incidents.

2.3. With respect to typhoons, classes shall be suspended upon advice of Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) whenever the typhoon is of sufficient intensity to make it advisable to suspend classes in the elementary grade and moreover when the approach of the typhoon becomes more definitely pronounced as to require suspension of classes in the high school and collegiate levels as well. Aside from such official announcements to be made, classes may be considered automatically suspended in the elementary grades when reports throughout the mass media confirm the raising of Typhoon Signals: No. 2 (suspension of classes in high school level); No. 3 (suspension of classes in the college level)

2.4. CHED Memorandum Order No. 15 series of 2012

2.4.1. Other force majeure and fortuitous events or circumstances which may compel immediate suspension of classes are fires, epidemics and bomb threats which will be dealt with accordingly as the occasion arises.

2.4.2.

SECTION: SAFETY GUIDE: WHAT TO DO IN AN EARTHQUAKE
SAFETY GUIDE: WHAT TO DO IN AN EARTHQUAKE
Source: general earthquake-safety guidance, NOT an LSPU-LB protocol. The campus's official evacuation areas and drill procedure were not supplied, so none are stated. Ask the Safety and Security Management Office.
During shaking: DROP to your hands and knees, take COVER under a sturdy desk or table (or protect your head and neck with your arms next to an inside wall), and HOLD ON until the shaking stops.
Stay away from windows, glass, shelves and heavy objects. If outdoors, move away from buildings, posts and wires. Do not run out during the shaking.
After it stops: leave the building calmly by the stairs (not the elevator) to an open area, expect aftershocks, and follow the guards and faculty.
Help others only if it is safe, and report injuries to a guard or the campus clinic. Call 911 for serious injuries or fire.

Sec. 2. Specific Guidelines

1. 1. Administrative Control Measures

1.1.1. Workspaces should be properly and regularly disinfected, ventilated, and maintained.

1.1.2. Putting of proper visual reminders for safety policies in strategic locations in the University to improve compliance.

1.1.3. Adoption and implementation of alternative work arrangements indicated in the Civil Service Commission Memorandum Circular 10, series of 2020.

1.2. Implementation of Other Prevention and Control Measures

1.2.1. There shall be health service personnel at the main gate to conduct daily temperature and symptom monitoring and recording of all employees who report to work. The health units are to submit weekly reports, or as the need arises to the Campus Director of their respective campus. They are to refer/report to RHU any probable or suspected case of

COVID-19.

EMERGENCY CONTACT: NATIONAL EMERGENCY HOTLINE 911
Source: general national information (not an LSPU document).
911 is the Philippine national emergency hotline. Call it for police, fire, ambulance and other urgent emergencies anywhere in the Philippines, including on or near the campus. Call it for a crime in progress, fire, serious injury or any life-threatening situation, then inform the campus guard as soon as you can.
